exposure: maternal body mass index (BMI) categorized as underweight, normal weight, overweight, and obese
outcome: admission to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)
cohort: The study included 110,057 pregnant women who gave birth at Mater Mother's Hospital Brisbane, Australia, between January 2008 and December 2019, with 17.08% of these women having asthma.
finding: Extremes of maternal BMI (underweight and obesity) significantly increased the risk of adverse perinatal outcomes, including stillbirth, neonatal death, perinatal death, and NICU admission, particularly in pregnancies complicated by asthma.
followup_time: Up to 28 days post-birth (for neonatal death outcome)
